statusNote: SCOPED 2026-07-30, awaiting Max's greenlight. Increment 7 of the HELM cockpit program — the first increment that puts the cockpit in the game. Max's four scoping decisions of 2026-07-30 are recorded in designDecisions: (1) the DOM overlay retirement happens HERE rather than after first light, taken AGAINST the recommendation to split it, with the risk stated and confirmed; (2) head decoupling is its own step right after; (3) all four cinematic autopilot paths route through the hands-off tour; (4) glass carries as-is with no refraction. The ORRERY answer the program demanded is decision (5): ORRERY keeps the two OPERABLE surfaces (nav computer, body info) and loses the flight readouts. ⚠ THE HIDDEN COST, surfaced at scoping and not yet priced: the cockpit's entire visual assembly — GLB load, scene, lights, eye camera, panel host, mover, picker — lives INLINE in cockpit-screens-lab.html and exists in no module. src/main.js contains only CockpitSnapshotProvider. So this increment must EXTRACT before it can wire.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The cockpit's visual assembly — GLB load, scene graph, lights, eye camera, panel host, mover, picker — is ONE module that both the lab and the game construct, not two copies. Today it is inline in cockpit-screens-lab.html and absent from src/; the lab must be converted to a caller of the shared rig, not left as a second implementation. This is the first AC because everything below depends on it, and because a second copy would drift: this workstream has been bitten five times by two instruments that disagreed, and 'the lab passes where the generator fails' is already a named failure mode in this program.

verifyVia.input: Import the rig module in a headless test and construct it against a stub renderer. Then grep the lab for the assembly calls the module now owns.
verifyVia.observable: The module constructs and exposes the panel records, the mover and the picker. The lab contains no remaining GLTFLoader/scene/light/mover/picker construction of its own — it calls the module. A planted divergence (change a light's intensity or the eye camera's fov in the module) shows up in BOTH the lab and the game rather than one of them.

verifyVia.observable: The cockpit's render pass is skipped entirely in ORRERY (not merely transparent — no pass, no cost), present in HELM, and present throughout the hands-off tour.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The four screens show real data about the flight Max is actually in, through the one read-only feed: DRIVE (speed/throttle/drive state/MODE), TARGET (selected target, distance, ETA, SAFE TO DROP), INFO (the selected body's physics), NAV (the nav computer). acceptanceCriteria.statement: A quick click works in the game — no press-and-hold. The game writes its own pointer routing from scratch (nothing in src/ builds a PanelHost today), so it must forward UNPRESSED pointer moves via PanelPointerAdapter.pointerHover or it reproduces the exact defect Max found at increment 6 UAT: NavComputer resolves every body in the map from hover state recomputed at DRAW time from _mouseX/_mouseY, which only _handleMouseMove writes. ⚠ AND THE PROBE MUST NOT HIDE IT AGAIN: clickGlass fires down → move → up, putting the move inside the gesture, which is what press-and-hold does by hand — that is why increment 6's live pass passed over this. Verification here must use a gesture with NOTHING between press and release.

verifyVia.input: With a panel zoomed in the game: move the cursor onto a planet with no button down, then press and release with no movement in between.
verifyVia.observable: The planet drills in. The pointer census shows the hover channel carrying the moves (hover count rising, pressed-move count zero) and lastRole is the zoomed panel. A control run with no preceding hover does nothing, proving the hover is what did the work.

designDecisions.decision: The DOM overlay retirement happens in increment 7, together with first light, rather than as a following increment.
designDecisions.why: Max chose it when asked. DIEGETIC-ONLY is his founding ruling and he did not want a period of double HUD.
designDecisions.recommendationWas: SPLIT — first light in increment 7 (cockpit renders, panels live, NAV interactive, overlays still present), retirement in increment 8. The stated risk: first light and demolition in one increment opens a second front across SupercruiseHud, BodyInfo, the NavComputer overlay and the 320² target circle while nothing has ever rendered in-game, it removes the overlay you would otherwise compare a wrong panel against, and it forces the ORRERY answer immediately. Max was told this and confirmed. Recorded so the trade-off is legible if the increment turns out large, not as a hedge.

designDecisions.decision: ORRERY keeps the nav computer and BodyInfo; SupercruiseHud, the 320² target circle and the debug physics rows retire in both modes.
designDecisions.why: The program's own ruling required the contract to give ORRERY-with-zero-HUD an answer rather than break it silently. Investigated before asking: the N key that opens the nav computer is NOT mode-gated (main.js:9695), so retiring it globally would leave ORRERY unable to pick a destination by hand — functional, not cosmetic. SupercruiseHud is already gated on `_scManual || scPilot.isActive`, so retiring it costs ORRERY nothing. The discriminator Max chose is OPERABLE vs READOUT: the readouts are HELM concepts and belong on the glass; the two machines you operate need a home in a mode with no cockpit.
designDecisions.notThe: This is NOT the 'split by mode' option rejected at program open. That option was the whole HUD coexisting with the cockpit. This is which mode hosts two operable surfaces, and it was put to Max as exactly that.

designDecisions.decision: The lab's inline cockpit assembly is extracted into a module both hosts construct, and the lab is converted to a caller. Taken without asking Max — it is an engineering call, not a product one.
designDecisions.why: The alternative is two copies of the GLB load, lights, eye camera and panel rig. This program has been bitten five times by two instruments that disagreed, and 'the lab passes where the generator fails' is already its named worst case. A second copy would also mean every future cockpit change gets made twice or silently once.
designDecisions.cost: This is the increment's hidden bulk and it was not in the handoff's four-item list. src/main.js contains only CockpitSnapshotProvider; PanelHost, PanelMover, PanelPicker, NavSource and NavPanel appear in it zero times.

designDecisions.decision: Head decoupling is its own step immediately after this increment. Glass carries as-is, with no screen-space refraction.
designDecisions.why: Decoupling is a feel knob wanting lab sliders and Max's eye; bundled, neither first light nor the decoupling can be judged cleanly, and a wrong time constant reads as 'the cockpit is broken'. Refraction was never built at all — increment 3's canopy is a plain mesh with a visibility toggle — and sampling the composited world is separate work that does not block flying. The cockpit still renders as its own pass, for the precision and resolution reasons, not only the refraction one.

openForMax: THE ARM — not in this increment, and not a knob. He wants it to 'realistically bend/extend along with the monitor moving'; the arm is one baked mesh with world-space vertices and no transform, so it needs re-authoring as segments in scripts/cockpit-gen.py plus a mover that drives them. Wants its own scoping conversation.
AC-NOTHING-I-HAD-GOT-LOST in cockpit-screen-content-2026-07-28 is still an open UAT gate. No agent can close it. It blocks that workstream's status flip, not this increment.
